primary.key: Fain to bring light to homes of men the noble and active Goddess hath emerged from darkness.
primary.s: A hymn to Dawn opens with the Daksina’s broad chariot harnessed and the immortal Gods aboard; Sāyaṇa, on 1.123.1, reads the Goddess’s purpose as healing, a cure she works on the dwellings of men by driving away the darkness of night.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.123.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 348392 (2022)

basis.words: अनन्तरं सा उषाः "कृष्णात् निकृष्टवर्णात् नैशात् तमसः सकाशात् "उदस्थात् उत्थिता अभूत् … मानुषाय "क्षयाय मनुष्याणां निवासाय “चिकित्सन्ती अन्धकारनिवारणरूपां चिकित्सां कुर्वती तमो निवारयन्तीत्यर्थः
basis.gloss: Then that Dawn rose up from ‘the black’, the base-coloured darkness of night … ‘for the human abode’, for the dwelling of men, ‘cikitsantī’: working a healing (cikitsā) whose form is the warding off of darkness; that is, she wards off the dark.

standby.key: The folk, O Mitra-Varuna, who hate you, who sinfully hating pour you no libations, Lay in their hearts, themselves, a wasting sickness, whereas the righteous gaineth all by worship.
standby.s: Turning to Mitra and Varuna in a hymn to all the Gods, the singer contrasts two kinds of men; Sāyaṇa, on 1.122.9, reads the heart’s sickness as the pain of seeing the good things enjoyed by those who keep the rite.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.122.9, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 205402 (2019)

basis.words: “सः मूढो द्विविधो जनः “स्वयं “यक्ष्मं व्याधिं “हृदये स्वचित्ते 'नि “धत्ते स्थापयति । अनुष्ठातॄणां भोगान् पश्यन् व्यथितो भवतीत्यर्थः ।
basis.gloss: That deluded man, of either kind, ‘himself’ places a yakṣma, a sickness, ‘in his heart’, in his own mind: seeing the enjoyments of those who perform the rite, he is pained; that is the meaning.

primary.key: Not interrupting heavenly ordinances, although she minisheth human generations. The last of endless morns that have departed, the first of those that come, Dawn brightly shineth.
primary.s: As the fire is kindled and Savitar sends all creatures to work, the hymn turns to Dawn’s dealings with Gods and men; Sāyaṇa, on 1.124.2, reads her as helping the Gods’ rites like the Agnihotra with her light while wearing away the life of men.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.124.2, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 368324 (2023)

basis.words: "दैव्यानि व्रतानि देवसंबन्धीनि अग्निहोत्रादीनि कर्माणि । … तानि कर्माणि "अमिनती अहिंसन्ती' भानप्रदानेनानुकूलं कुर्वती । तथा "मनुष्या मनुष्याणां "युगानि युगोपलक्षितान् निमेषादिकालावयवान् “प्रमिनती प्रकर्षेण हिंसन्ती आयुः क्षपयन्तीत्यर्थः ।
basis.gloss: ‘The divine ordinances’ (vratas): rites belonging to the gods, the Agnihotra and the rest … those rites she does not harm (aminatī) but makes favourable by giving light; and ‘the yugas of men’: the divisions of time the yugas stand for, the blink of an eye and the rest, she destroys outright (praminatī); that is, she wears away their life.

standby.key: Near is she seen, as ’twere the Bright One’s bosom: she showeth sweet things like a new song-singer.
standby.s: A hymn to Dawn gathers likenesses for her rising in the east; Yāska, Nirukta 4.16, takes the ‘Bright One’ as the Sun, named from purifying, and the singer as a seer who makes his wishes plain in praise, as Dawn makes her forms plain.
standby.src: Yāska, Nirukta 4.16, trans. Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1920 to 1921)

basis.words: The pure one is the sun, (so called) from … Nodha, (singer) means a seer: he composes .1 new hymn. As he makes his desires apparent in his songs of praise so dawn manifests her beauteous forms.
basis.gloss: The pure one (śundhyu, the Bright One) is the sun, so called from purifying … Nodhas (the singer) means a seer: he composes a new hymn. As he makes his desires plain in his songs of praise, so Dawn makes her lovely forms plain. (Sarup’s OCR prints “.1” for “a”.)

primary.key: Couples desirous of thine aid are storming thee, pouring their presents forth to win a stall of kine, pouring gifts, Indra, seeking thee.
primary.s: With Heaven and Earth bowed to Indra, the hymn turns to those who worship him; Sāyaṇa, on 1.131.3, reads the ‘couples’ as husbands and wives, holding that a wife may share the rite with her husband, though not perform it alone.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.131.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 207804 (2019)

basis.words: “मिथुनाः पत्नीसहिता यजमानाः “वि ततस्रे यज्ञं वितन्वते । … यद्यपि स्त्रियाः नास्ति पृथगधिकारस्तथापि पूर्वमीमांसायां षष्ठेऽधिकाराध्याये तृतीयचतुर्थाभ्यामधिकरणाभ्यां अस्त्येव स्त्रिया अधिकारः स च पत्या सहेति प्रपञ्चितत्वात् … तस्मात् मिथुना यज्ञं ततस्रे इत्येतत् युक्तम् ।
basis.gloss: ‘The couples’: sacrificers together with their wives, ‘spread out’ (vi tatasre) the sacrifice … Although a woman has no separate right, yet, since the Pūrva Mīmāṃsā, in its sixth book, on qualification, sets out in its third and fourth sections that a woman does have a right, and that together with her husband … therefore ‘the couples spread out the sacrifice’ is fitting.

standby.key: Ride hither to the offering of the pleasant juice, the holy Fig-tree which victorious priests surround: victorious be they still for us.
standby.s: A hymn calling Vayu and Indra to the pressed Soma nears its close, promising Vayu cows that never run dry; Sāyaṇa, on 1.135.8, takes the ‘Fig-tree’ as the Soma itself, standing on the mountains, which victorious sacrificers gather round to buy.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.135.8, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 226442 (2020)

basis.words: “यं सोमम् “अश्वत्थं पर्वतादिव्याप्तिप्रदेशे स्थितं "जायवः जेतारो यजमानाः “उपतिष्ठन्त उपेत्य तिष्ठन्ति क्रयाद्यर्थम् ।
basis.gloss: ‘Which’ Soma, ‘the aśvattha’ (the Fig-tree), standing in the places it spreads over, mountains and the like, ‘the victorious ones’, the conquering sacrificers, ‘surround’: they approach and attend on it, for its purchase and the like.
